title: Deal Into Two Piles by Top Card
statement:
You deal the distinct numbers in nums one by one onto two piles, left and right.

  • The first number starts left, the second number starts right.
  • Every later number goes onto the pile whose top card (the number placed on it most recently) is larger. Since all numbers differ, there is never a tie.

When all numbers are dealt, return the left pile followed by the right pile, each in the order its cards were placed.

examples.why: 8 goes left (top 5 beats top 2). 1 goes left (top 8 beats 2). 9 goes right, because left's top is now 1, even though left holds the biggest card so far.
1 joins left (6 > 3). Now left's top is 1, so 5 and 4 both go right.
Right's top 2 beats left's 1, so 3 goes right. The rule compares tops, never the incoming number.

constraints: All values in nums are distinct
hints: This is a direct simulation. What do you need to remember about each pile to place the next card?
Only each pile's last element matters for the decision.
Keep two arrays; for i ≥ 2, push nums[i] to whichever array has the larger last element; return left.concat(right).

explain.intuition:
There is no trick here: the rule tells you exactly what to do, and the job is to follow it precisely. The decision for each card depends only on the two current top cards, so keep both piles as arrays and read their last elements.

Easy simulations are where small misreadings cost the most in interviews. The common slips are comparing the new card instead of the tops, or comparing whole piles (their largest or first card) instead of the top cards.
steps: For each i ≥ 2: if the last element of left is larger than the last of right, push nums[i] to left, otherwise to right.
pitfalls: Comparing the pile maxima or the first cards instead of the most recent ones. In the first example 9 would wrongly go left.
Comparing the incoming number with a top card instead of the two tops with each other.
Returning the piles interleaved, or right before left.

solutions.title: Two arrays
solutions.idea: Simulate with two arrays and compare their last elements before each push.

solutions.title: Track only the tops and a side label
solutions.idea: Record which pile each card went to while keeping just the two top values, then rebuild the answer from the labels.

followups: Change the rule: a card goes to the pile holding more cards that are larger than it. Which data structure answers "how many larger" quickly?
Can you produce the answer in place inside nums, without the second array?
